"A weekend hackathon on scientific parallelism, about 30 hours, on 21 November. GPUs are provided; their type is not yet
known. Teams may bring their own problem, and the thinking, data and baseline can be prepared beforehand.

Judges score reshaping, a credible baseline, correctness and scientific value. A carefully explained failure to get a
speedup can still win, if its failure modes were predicted in advance.

The sponsors build systems that split workloads into subtasks and route each to the best chip, and low-latency
inference chips. The question they care about: which parts of a workload are sequential, and must they be?

Propose five projects for this hackathon, from any field of science. For each give: title; field; sequential_part, the part of the work that one answer waits on step after step, or \"none\"; restructure, how your project changes that (or what it runs in parallel); condition, what must hold for it to pay off; baselines, what the result is timed and checked against; first_test, the cheapest measurement to run first and its rough cost. Decide from what you know; do not use tools.

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"proposals\"],\"properties\":{\"proposals\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"title\",\"field\",\"sequential_part\",\"restructure\",\"condition\",\"baselines\",\"first_test\"],\"properties\":{\"title\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"field\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"sequential_part\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"restructure\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"condition\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"baselines\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"first_test\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"

We need answer JSON only. Need propose five projects for hackathon. Need follow schema. Need think carefully. We have no tools. Need five projects from any field science. For each title, field, sequential_part, restructure, condition, baselines, first_test. Content should be plausible and diverse. Need ensure valid JSON. We can only output JSON object.

Let's craft five proposals. Need include sequential part as "none" possible. Restructure. Condition. Baselines. First_test with rough cost.

Need maybe fields: computational biology, molecular dynamics, climate, astrophysics, quantum chemistry, materials, genomics, fluid dynamics? Need five.

Important prompt: weekend hackathon scientific parallelism, GPUs. Judges score reshaping, credible baseline, correctness and scientific value. Failure can win with predicted modes. Sponsors split workloads into subtasks route to best chip, low-latency inference. Question: which parts sequential must they be? Projects should reflect sequential_part analysis.

Let's design robust proposals.

Proposal 1: Adaptive step molecular dynamics with speculative parallel force evaluation? sequential part: neighbor list updates and time integration? Restructure: replace sequential Verlet integration with speculative parallel multiple time stepping, run fast/slow force kernels concurrently. But maybe.

Better: Field computational materials. Title "Speculative parallel replica exchange for protein folding". sequential_part: "Replica exchange attempts are conditionally accepted one after another, and exchange decisions depend on previous swaps" perhaps. Restructure: evaluate all neighboring exchange probabilities independently in parallel and use deterministic conflict resolution (graph coloring) to decouple. Condition: exchange acceptance rates low enough that conflicts are rare/cheap, GPUs enough. Baselines: serial GROMACS replica exchange, OpenMM. First_test: "Time 32-replica alanine dipeptide exchange with and without coloring on one GPU; expected ~30 min."

Or make sequential part clear.

Proposal 2: Field climate/atmospheric science. Title "Parallel in time data assimilation for storm-scale weather". Sequential part: 4D-Var adjoint model runs forward then backward serially through assimilation window. Restructure: Parareal/PFASST parallel-in-time splitting into coarse propagator and fine local solves across GPUs. Condition: parallel-in-time convergence faster than serial adjoint for limited windows; coarse model accurate enough. Baselines: serial 4D-Var or EnKF implementation. First_test: "Run 10-timestep Lorenz96 assimilation comparison, ~$0.10 GPU-hour."

Proposal 3: Field genomics. Title "Speculative k-mer graph assembly for long reads". sequential_part: "de Bruijn graph traversal/contig extension is inherently sequential path walking." Restructure: split graph into weakly connected components; perform speculative branch resolution in parallel, commit according to read coverage. Condition: graph components small enough and branching limited so parallel speculative extension avoids incorrect contigs. Baselines: current assembler (minimap2+SPAdes or Flye) accurate contigs. First_test: "Assemble E. coli 5 Mb long-read set with branch speculation depth 2 vs baseline; ~15 min on one GPU."

But maybe field computational biology.

Proposal 4: Field astrophysics cosmology. Title "Parallel N-body halo finder with asynchronous linking". Sequential part: friends-of-friends linking uses iterative label propagation where labels cascade through chains in serial order. Restructure: use union-find with pointer jumping in parallel on GPU, resolving chains by tree contraction. Condition: high dynamic range halos produce long chains; enough memory bandwidth for atomic union-find. Baselines: serial FoF/ROCKSTAR halo catalogs. First_test: "Halo find on 10^7 particle test box vs ROCKSTAR, cost under $1 GPU-hour."

Proposal 5: Field quantum chemistry. Title "Parallel contraction for coupled-cluster tensor amplitudes". sequential part: iterative amplitude equations have update order and contractions that can serialize over occupied/virtual indices. Restructure: fused GPU tensor contractions over distributed GPUs with asynchronous communication, reorder equations with algebraic transformations (factorization) to expose parallelism. Condition: tensor dimensions exceed GPU memory, but equation can be refactored to reduce intermediate serial dependencies. Baselines: PySCF/CCSD or NWChem TCE. First_test: "Time one CCSD iteration on 4 GPUs for a (H2O) cluster with cc-pVDZ vs single node; cost ~$2 GPU-hour."

Need maybe include "none" sequential part in one? The prompt asks sequential_part "the part ... or none". We can include "none" maybe for embarrassingly parallel. But projects should analyze sequential part. Maybe one project with none: "Monte Carlo ensemble" no sequential part. But judges want which parts sequential and must they be. Could include a proposal where sequential_part none to show. Let's maybe include 5 with one none: field high-energy physics? "Independent event generation for collider physics" sequential_part none. But baselines etc. Yet hackathon about parallelism. However they want five projects. We can have one "none" to contrast. But maybe all should include a sequential_part. The field can be any. Need robust.

Let's maybe design five with clear sequential_part:

1. Protein folding / molecular dynamics: "Sequential time integration and neighbor-list rebuild barriers between steps; force evaluation is already parallel but step-to-step dependency remains." Restructure: "Multiple time stepping with speculative fast forces: compute slow forces and several fast-force substeps concurrently using extrapolated positions; roll back on rare clashes." Condition: "slow/fast force separation valid and rollback rate low (<5%)". Baselines: "OpenMM serial CPU/GPU integration, exact 2fs Verlet." First_test: "Time 1 ns of DHFR (23k atoms) with speculative 4fs/1fs split vs baseline on one GPU, ~15 min, metric: steps/sec and energy drift."

2. Climate / parallel-in-time: "Sequential forward and adjoint model in 4D-Var optimization loop." Restructure: "replace serial window integration with ParaExp / PFASST: coarse propagator corrects fine parallel chunks per iteration." Condition: "coarse model error small enough for parallel-in-time iteration to converge in few passes; GPUs have enough memory for multiple time slices." Baselines: serial adjoint integration, L-BFGS convergence." First_test: "Lorenz-96 40-variable, 100-step window: compare wall-clock and analysis RMSE, ~$0.05 GPU-hour."

3. Genomics assembly: "Contig extension walks one branch at a time; order of extension depends on previous read support." Restructure: "speculative branch extension with bidirectional de Bruijn graph peels in parallel; resolve conflicts via read depth voting." Condition: "short-read coverage > 30x and repeat branches short enough to speculate; wrong branch rollback cheap." Baselines: "Spades contigs / Flye unitigs on E. coli." First_test: "Assemble 5 Mb E. coli 100x paired reads with speculative branching vs baseline; wall clock and N50; ~20 min one GPU."

4. Astrophysics halo finding: "Friends-of-friends label propagation through particle chains is iterative and can serialize over dense filaments." Restructure: "GPU union-find with pointer-jumping / tree contraction; each block merges labels in parallel, then global resolution via atomic compare-and-swap." Condition: "enough HBM bandwidth and atomics; halo catalogs don't require exact per-step propagation order." Baselines: "ROCKSTAR or serial FoF on same particle box." First_test: "10^7 particle dark matter box: compute halo masses and compare; <1 GPU-hour."

5. Quantum chemistry coupled cluster: "Coupled-cluster amplitude update: each iteration requires sequential contraction of tensors with no obvious DAG parallelism; naive ordering serial." Restructure: "algebraic tensor factorization and persistent kernels; split occupied/virtual indices across GPUs and overlap communication with computation." Condition: "factorized intermediates preserve numerical accuracy and reduce critical path; network latency not dominant." Baselines: "PySCF CCSD one iteration on CPU/single GPU." First_test: "Time one CCSD iteration on 4 GPUs for H2O cluster cc-pVDZ vs single GPU; ~30 min."

Let's write. Need ensure "first_test" includes rough cost. Include "$0.05 GPU-hour" etc. Fine.

Double-check each proposal.

Proposal 1 details:
title: "Speculative multiple-timestep molecular dynamics for protein systems"
field: "computational biophysics"
sequential_part: "The Verlet time integrator advances one step at a time; slow force evaluations and neighbor-list rebuilds create a step-to-step serial barrier despite parallel force kernels."
restructure: "Run fast bonded/nonbonded substeps concurrently with one speculative slow force evaluation using extrapolated positions; commit substeps and roll back only when a rare collision or large-force rejection triggers a resimulation."
condition: "Slow and fast forces are separable and the speculative rejection rate stays low (roughly <5%), so rollback recomputation costs less than serial slow-force steps."
baselines: "Reference 2 fs Verlet integration in OpenMM/AMBER on one GPU; timings and energy drift compared for equivalence."
first_test: "Time 1 ns of DHFR (about 23k atoms) with a 4 fs slow / 1 fs fast split against baseline on one GPU; ~15-30 min, report steps/sec, rollback rate, and energy drift."

Good.

Proposal 2:
title: "Parallel-in-time adjoint data assimilation for storm-scale weather"
field: "climate science / numerical weather prediction"
sequential_part: "4D-Var requires integrating the forecast forward and the adjoint backward through the entire assimilation window one timestep at a time, with the adjoint path itself serially dependent."
restructure: "Use ParaExp/PFASST-style parallel-in-time splitting: a coarse propagator provides initial values so fine timestep chunks integrate concurrently on multiple GPUs, and corrections iterate only where coarse error is large."
condition: "The coarse model is accurate enough that parallel-in-time iterations converge in few passes; enough GPU memory holds multiple time slices simultaneously."
baselines: "Serial 4D-Var or ensemble Kalman smoother on the same test case, comparing wall-clock, convergence, and analysis RMSE."
first_test: "Lorenz-96 40-variable, 100-timestep window: compare wall-clock and analysis error between serial adjoint and parallel-in-time; roughly $0.05 GPU-hour."

Proposal 3:
title: "Speculative branching for de Bruijn graph genome assembly"
field: "genomics / computational biology"
sequential_part: "Contig extension walks the assembly graph one supported edge at a time, and the choice at each branch depends on previously committed sequence."
restructure: "Peel the de Bruijn graph in parallel across independent components, and speculatively extend multiple branches at each fork; commit the branch with best read-depth and mismatch support, rolling back alternatives."
condition: "Sequencing coverage is high (e.g. >30x) and repeat-induced branches are short enough that speculative alternatives can be enumerated cheaply and resolved by read evidence."
baselines: "SPAdes or Flye contigs/unitigs on the same reads, measured by wall-clock and N50/identity."
first_test: "Assemble 5 Mb E. coli reads at 100x coverage with speculative branch depth two versus baseline; ~20 min on one GPU; compare N50, contig length, and runtime."

Proposal 4:
title: "Parallel friends-of-friends halo finding via GPU union-find"
field: "astrophysics / cosmology"
sequential_part: "Friends-of-friends groups are found by propagating labels through chains of linked particles; on dense filaments that propagation can become a long serial cascade."
restructure: "Replace label propagation with union-find plus pointer jumping/tree contraction: GPU blocks merge edges in parallel, then resolve parent chains via atomic compare-and-swap until roots stabilize."
condition: "Group chains and GPU atomics are handled efficiently in high-bandwidth memory; approximate grouping order is sufficient for scientific halo catalogs."
baselines: "Serial FoF and/or ROCKSTAR on the same dark-matter particle box, comparing halo mass function and positions."
first_test: "Run group finding on a 10^7-particle test box and compare halo counts and masses to baseline; under about 1 GPU-hour."

Proposal 5:
title: "Reducing the serial contraction path in iterative coupled-cluster amplitude equations"
field: "quantum chemistry"
sequential_part: "Coupled-cluster amplitude updates have many tensor contractions whose naive order forms a long serial dependence chain, so each iteration is limited by critical path latency."
restructure: "Use algebraic tensor factorization and persistent kernels to flatten the contraction DAG; distribute occupied/virtual blocks across GPUs and overlap communication with compute to shorten critical path."
condition: "Factorized intermediates preserve numerical accuracy to within convergence tolerance, and interconnect latency is small relative to contracted tensor sizes."
baselines: "PySCF or NWChem CCSD iteration on CPU and single-GPU, checked by energy and amplitude convergence."
first_test: "Time one CCSD iteration for a water cluster with cc-pVDZ on 4 GPUs versus single GPU; ~30 min and a few GPU-hours at most."

Need verify all required keys exactly. Could include field "climate science / numerical weather prediction". Field is string. Fine. But maybe avoid slash? It's string. No issue.

Need JSON only. Ensure $ signs okay. Within JSON strings, "$" no escape necessary. Use "~" etc.

Let's produce final JSON one line.

Check if quotes in "e.g." maybe no. Fine. Need avoid backslash? "de Bruijn" okay. "4D-Var" okay.

Potential issue: apostrophe? In "friends-of-friends" no. "cc-pVDZ" fine.

Let's final with JSON.

But before final, perhaps consider if first_test cost rough "about 1 GPU-hour" etc. Good.
